slides.notes: Open with the decision: authorize a governed pilot, not broad adoption. The walkthrough demonstrates choice architecture, not measured business impact.
Separate observed mechanisms from the proposed decision. The three mechanisms justify testing, while every outcome claim remains unproven.
The cost problem is directional debt. Fast generation has limited value when teams correct macro direction only after implementation begins.
Use the interface state as proof of visible macro choice. Require a named owner and recorded rationale before variants are built.
The feature count is incidental. Divergence produces value only when commitment gates stop rerolls and move the work forward.
A narrow workflow can be the better choice. Generality raises differentiation and operator variance at the same time.
Route by change altitude. Live is for bounded detail; terminal work changes structure; references reopen direction.
Live Mode is valuable after direction is accepted. Do not use faster local iteration to rationalize weak visual grammar.
A reference is a controlled reset mechanism, not decoration. Record provenance and the grammar being borrowed.

Allocate reversible work to the system and irreversible judgment to accountable people: truth, direction, trade-offs, and release. Release requires an independent fresh-context human check; system detection is support, not adjudication.
The design record can reduce reinvention, but it must be versioned and explicitly resettable so stale taste does not become policy.
Do not translate workflow sophistication into outcome certainty. Productivity, usability, quality, and commercial effects remain pilot hypotheses.
Hold inputs and operator profiles constant and blind downstream reviewers. Count major direction resets before acceptance as the primary endpoint.
Close on three actions: name the owner, select the bounded task, and lock the scorecard before any showcase output is reviewed.
